Advertisement View all journals Saved research Search Account Log in Content Explore content About the journal Publish with us Subscribe Sign up for alerts RSS feed nature nature water articles article Article Published: 01 September 2026 Coupling filter mating with nanopore selective sequencing expands capturable conjugative plasmid recovery in biological wastewater treatment systems Yuxi Yan ORCID: orcid.org/0009-0001-9495-9882 1 , 2 , Ziqi Wu 1 , Yuhong Sun 1 , Miao Zhang 1 , Bixi Zhao 1 , Cailong Nie ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0002-7052-3195 1 , Zhanwen Cheng 1 , Qing Yang 1 , Liming Chen 1 , Qiqi Hao ORCID: orcid.org/0009-0001-0481-4824 3 , Bing Fu 3 & … Yu Xia ORCID: orcid.org/0000-0003-2842-6639 1 , 4 , 5 Show authors Nature Water ( 2026 ) Cite this article Save article View saved research 124 Accesses Metrics details Abstract Wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) are hotspots for the exchange of plasmids, which can spread antibiotic resistance genes. However, recovering conjugative plasmids from complex communities remains challenging because both plasmid extraction and cultivation-based approaches introduce bias. Here we show that filter mating coupled with nanopore selective sequencing (FM-NSS) can recover an ampicillin-selected, recipient-compatible fraction of conjugative plasmids from a full-scale WWTP without plasmid extraction. After depletion of reads aligning to the Escherichia coli recipient genome, FM-NSS recovered a total of 1.10 million plasmid reads. De novo assembly yielded 622 non-redundant plasmid contigs, including 441 not detected by extraction-based plasmid sequencing from the same conjugant pools. Notably, activated sludge displayed a distinct recovered plasmid profile compared with other treatment stages, which is associated with an elevated estimation of community replication rates. FM-NSS provides a practical workflow to expand the recovery of selected conjugative plasmids from complex environmental communities.
